sensor_refs[SPY-1D(V)].note: DDG-96 Bainbridge carries SPY-1D(V) per OOB; DDG-81 Winston S. Churchill (this variant's other named hull) carries baseline SPY-1D. This record uses the SPY-1D(V) sensor as representative since Flight IIA includes both DDG-81 (D) and DDG-96 (D(V)); documented as a simplification for a class-level record

modeling_notes: Health scaled as one HP per metric tonne of full-load displacement, per the repo's existing DDG-51/T-AKE convention.

VLS mounts abstract the mixed SM-2/SM-6/ESSM/Tomahawk/VL-ASROC load into two generic vls_sam mounts (fwd 32-cell, aft 64-cell) per the authoring standard's 3-functional-mount-type rule; individual missile kinematics/warheads in weapons/csg/us/*.json do not directly drive vls_sam mount behavior (see weapon record provenance for the engine mechanism-gap note).

Tomahawk, Maritime Strike Tomahawk, VL-ASROC, and Mk 54 torpedoes have no NavalWeaponType mount and are listed only in _real_world.weapon_inventory with status content_only_no_mechanism, per the authoring standard's mechanism-gap rule.
Representative VLS loadout (40 SM-2 + 16 SM-6 + 32 ESSM + 24 Tomahawk + 8 VL-ASROC = 96 cells with ESSM quad-packed) is Tier est per OOB; actual loadouts are never published.

Added a 4th hitbox (hangar/flight_deck/helo_fuel) beyond the repo's 3-zone DDG-51 Flight I MVP pattern to give the embarked MH-60R aviation facility its own damageable zone, consistent with the task's instruction that each ship needs explicit hitboxes naming real systems; this is a structural addition, not a value change to existing zones.

damage_model.hitboxes[].components[] uses only name/system per the real DamageComponent schema confirmed against unit_definition_loader.cpp (~line 1273-1320) and the repo's f16c_block50.json example; components have no per-component hp field (health is tracked at ship level via health.current_hp/max_hp), so no hp values were invented. Optional threshold_scale/mechanism_thresholds/redundancy_group_id fields are omitted since no sourced or calibrated basis exists for CSG-specific values beyond what the task requires (component naming for real systems).

DDG-81 (Winston S. Churchill) has 2 Phalanx mounts per OOB; DDG-85 and later (including DDG-96 Bainbridge) have only 1 aft. This record includes a single phalanx_ciws mount as the class-representative baseline; a second CIWS mount for DDG-81 specifically is not separately instantiated here since this is a class-level (not per-hull) record per the authoring standard's naming convention.
